## Doruk İlkay İlaç Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. — VENZY, TR · AE · QA · SA

- one: Identical mark, Class 5, actively marketed as a prescription medicine in TR/UAE/QA/SA — proceed only after confirming whether the client intends to sell in any of those markets.

### The read
Doruk İlkay holds VENZY as a registered Class 5 pharmaceutical mark in Turkey and the UAE, with applications pending in Qatar and Saudi Arabia, and uses it on a marketed prescription product (solifenacin succinate, a urinary antispasmodic) across those territories. Under the framework established in *Canon* and confirmed in *SABEL* and *Stada (RUXXIMLA)*, identical word marks on Class 5 prescription goods sold through the same pharmacy channel are confusable regardless of therapeutic-area divergence — the channel overlap and shared patient population satisfy the goods-relatedness test, and an identical mark leaves no similarity gap to weigh in the client's favour. On the available signals — a five-registration portfolio spanning four jurisdictions, two of which are still active prosecution fronts — Doruk İlkay appears likely to object if the client markets under the same name in any covered territory, though no filed enforcement action against a third party has been verified on this record.

### Full detail
- **Mark and use.** Doruk İlkay's VENZY is a live prescription product: solifenacin succinate (urinary antispasmodic), marketed in Turkey, UAE, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia — confirmed via the Abu Dhabi DoH reference price list and İlaç Rehberi (İlaç Rehberi is the Turkish pharmaceutical registry).
- **Portfolio.** Five registrations/applications across TR, AE, QA, and SA, all in Class 5; the 2024 Turkish filing additionally covers Class 35. The two TR filings and the SA filing are pending; the TR 2009 and AE filings are registered and valid.
- **Jurisdiction note.** Registered rights sit in TR, AE, QA, and SA — none is an EU member state. Turkish Industrial Property Law No. 6769 (2017) is broadly harmonised with the EU Trade Mark Directive (2015/2436/EU), making CJEU/General Court doctrine persuasive for the Turkish confusion analysis. AE, QA, and SA operate under their own national regimes; EU doctrine does not apply there directly, and those jurisdictions represent a coverage gap for local-law analysis.
- **Confusability.** The marks are identical — there is no visual, aural, or conceptual dissimilarity to weigh. Under *SABEL* (C-251/95), the global-impression analysis favours the earlier owner where marks are identical. Under *Canon* (C-39/97), goods in the same distribution channel and directed at overlapping patient populations satisfy goods-relatedness; therapeutic-area divergence (bladder antispasmodic vs. the client's goods) goes to degree of similarity, not to the existence of overlap. *Stada (T-239/20)* confirmed that even partial letter overlap (6/8 shared letters) was sufficient for confusion across Class 5 pharmaceuticals — identical marks set the ceiling.
- **Enforcer.** No filed opposition, cancellation, or litigation by Doruk İlkay against a third party has been verified on this record. On the available signals — a multi-jurisdiction portfolio with an active 2024 refiling in Turkey — the owner appears likely to monitor and object to an identical mark entering the same channel, but this remains an inference from portfolio behaviour, not a confirmed enforcement posture.
- [internal] Goods similarity basis is verified from the Corsearch register record (TR 2009 filing, Class 5); mark similarity basis is inferred from the identical-word signal; enforcer basis is inferred from portfolio signals, not a verified filing.
- **If enforced:** Identical mark on a marketed medicine; if Doruk İlkay enforced in a MENA market where the client sells, exposure is name-change, relabelling, and re-registration in TR/UAE/QA/SA — not the major markets, which are clear. Scale and reversibility depend on whether the client actually markets under VENZY in those countries — a fact only the client holds — for the client to weigh.
